overview.headline: Early confederation government and its replacement

keyPoints.point: Students learn the Articles of Confederation were adopted by the Continental Congress on November 15, 1777 and served as the first constitution until 1789.
keyPoints.quote: The Articles of Confederation were adopted by the Continental Congress on November 15, 1777.

keyPoints.point: Students learn John Dickinson was the principal writer for the committee formed to determine the form of confederation.
keyPoints.quote: John Dickinson, a delegate from Delaware, was the principal writer.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the Confederation outlined a Congress with representation not based on population where each state would have one vote.
keyPoints.quote: The Articles of Confederation also outlined a Congress with representation not based on population – each state would have one vote in Congress.

keyPoints.point: Students learn when Maryland ratified on March 1, 1781 the Congress of the Confederation came into being after delays over western lands.
keyPoints.quote: When Maryland ratified it on March 1, 1781, the Congress of the Confederation came into being.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the central government had insufficient power to regulate commerce, could not tax, and faced depleted treasury and extraordinary inflation.
keyPoints.quote: With the states retaining considerable power, the central government had insufficient power to regulate commerce.

keyTerms.gloss: body that appointed committees to design confederation plan
keyTerms.quote: the Second Continental Congress appointed three committees on June 11, 1776.

keyTerms.gloss: delegate from Delaware who was principal writer of draft
keyTerms.quote: John Dickinson, a delegate from Delaware, was the principal writer.

keyTerms.gloss: established alliance for sovereign and independent states
keyTerms.quote: This "first constitution of the United States" established a "league of friendship" for the 13 sovereign and independent states.

keyTerms.gloss: necessary approval by all states to set Confederation into motion
keyTerms.quote: Ratification by all 13 states was necessary to set the Confederation into motion.

keyTerms.gloss: assembled in Philadelphia in May 1787 to revise Articles
keyTerms.quote: In May of 1787, the Constitutional Convention assembled in Philadelphia to revise the Articles of Confederation.
